question: I used all my TFSA contribution room and then withdrew $2,000 during the current calendar year. Can I automatically contribute that $2,000 back immediately, and when does the withdrawal become new room?
generated_answer:
In Canada, the Tax-Free Savings Account (TFSA) program allows you to withdraw funds at any time, but the rules for re-contributing those funds can be a bit nuanced.

When you withdraw $2,000 from your TFSA during the current calendar year, you cannot immediately re-contribute that amount back into your TFSA in the same year, unless you have available contribution room.

The withdrawn amount of $2,000 will be added back to your TFSA contribution room at the beginning of the next calendar year. This means that on January 1st of the following year, your TFSA contribution room will increase by the amount you withdrew ($2,000), allowing you to re-contribute that amount if you wish.

To illustrate this:

* You contribute the maximum allowed to your TFSA and use up all your available contribution room.
* You then withdraw $2,000 from your TFSA during the current calendar year.
* You cannot re-contribute the $2,000 immediately, as you have no available contribution room left for the current year.
* On January 1st of the next calendar year, the $2,000 you withdrew will be added back to your TFSA contribution room, along with any other new contribution room you may be eligible for (e.g., the annual TFSA contribution limit).
* At this point, you can re-contribute the $2,000, as well as make any other contributions you're eligible for, up to your new total available contribution room.

It's essential to keep track of your TFSA contributions and withdrawals to avoid over-contributing, which can result in penalties and interest charges from the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA). If you're unsure about your TFSA contribution room or have questions about re-contributing withdrawn funds, consider consulting with a financial advisor or contacting the CRA directly.
